headline: Disney+ and Hulu bundle drops to $4.99 a month for a year in a Black Friday deal that ends Nov 30
tldr: Disney+'s Black Friday offer cuts the ad-supported Disney+, Hulu Bundle from $12.99 to $4.99 a month for 12 months (Premium: $14.99, from $21.99). New and eligible returning subscribers only; ends Nov 30.
who: People in the U.S. who don't currently subscribe to Disney+, Hulu, ESPN or a bundle and are thinking about the Disney+, Hulu Bundle; current subscribers are excluded
seo_title: Disney+ Black Friday 2026: Disney+, Hulu Bundle $4.99/mo for a year (ends Nov 30)
seo_desc: Disney+'s Black Friday 2026 deal: the ad-supported Disney+, Hulu Bundle is $4.99 a month for 12 months, then $12.99; Premium is $14.99 for 12 months, then $21.99. Ends 11:59 PM PST Nov 30. Current subscribers aren't eligible.

redline.after: Disney+, Hulu Bundle, which includes Disney+ (With Ads) and Hulu (With Ads), is
redline.label: Disney+ home page · Bundle plans
redline.note: The bundle copy switches from a 6-month offer to a Black Friday price.

redline.label: Plan table · Disney+, Hulu Bundle, monthly price
redline.note: Down from $11.99 a month for six months to $4.99 a month for twelve, against the regular $12.99.

redline.label: Plan table · Disney+, Hulu Bundle Premium, monthly price
redline.note: The no-ads Premium bundle is $14.99 for a year, against the regular $21.99.

actions: If you don't subscribe now and want the bundle, sign up on disneyplus.com before 11:59 PM PST on November 30, 2026
Set a reminder for 12 months after you sign up: the price "auto-renews at $12.99/mo. or then-current regular monthly price" ($21.99 for Premium)
Don't switch plans after signing up: Disney's terms say "Any plan switch after redemption of this offer will result in forfeiture of the discount pricing"
what:
Disney+'s [home page](https://www.disneyplus.com/) now leads with a Black Friday offer: the Disney+, Hulu Bundle "is $12.99/mo $4.99/mo for a year this Black Friday. Offer ends November 30", and the Disney+, Hulu Bundle Premium (no ads) is $14.99 a month for a year, down from $21.99 (fetched November 24, 2026). The plan table's "Black Friday Offer" badges show "Save 61%" and "Save 31%".

## The fine print (Disney+ offer terms, fetched Nov 24)

Disney's terms say: "Disney+, Hulu Bundle: $4.99/mo. for 12 mos., then auto-renews at $12.99/mo. or then-current regular monthly price. Disney+, Hulu Bundle Premium: $14.99/mo. for 12 mos., then auto-renews at $21.99/mo. or then-current regular monthly price. Ends 11:59 PM PST on 11/30/26. U.S. only, 18+. New and eligible returning subscribers only." They add: "Valid for new and eligible returning subscribers; Disney+, ESPN, Hulu, and bundle subscribers are not eligible." and "Any plan switch after redemption of this offer will result in forfeiture of the discount pricing." The offer is "not redeemable via gift card" and can't be combined with a free trial or other promotions.

Our math: 12 months at $4.99 is $59.88, against $155.88 at the regular $12.99, a saving of $96. Premium: $179.88 for the year against $263.88, a saving of $84.

What it replaces: Until November 23 the same page offered the bundle at "$11.99 / mo for 6 months" (Premium "$19.99 / mo for 6 months"), with a "Cost for 6 months: $71.94, then renews to monthly plan at $12.99/month" footnote, and a student offer of the bundle for "$6.49/mo". Both are no longer shown on the home page; the page doesn't say whether they return after November 30.

What stays the same: The regular prices ($12.99 with ads, $21.99 Premium) are unchanged, as are the ESPN Unlimited bundles ($35.99 and $44.99 a month) and the Disney+, Hulu, HBO Max bundles ($21.99 with ads, $34.99 no ads).
faq: Can current Disney+ or Hulu subscribers get the $4.99 Black Friday deal?
No. Disney's offer terms say "Disney+, ESPN, Hulu, and bundle subscribers are not eligible." It is for new and eligible returning subscribers in the U.S., 18+.
What does the Disney+, Hulu Bundle cost after the Black Friday year?
It "auto-renews at $12.99/mo. or then-current regular monthly price". Premium renews at $21.99 or the then-current price.
When does the Disney+ Black Friday deal end?
11:59 PM PST on November 30, 2026, per the offer terms.
sources: Disney+ home page and Black Friday offer terms (fetched Nov 24, 2026)

headline: Discord's Dec 15 terms let server admins show server content in search engine results
tldr: Discord's updated terms, in force December 15, say admins can have server content "appear off of Discord (such as in search engine results)", and hand all arbitrability questions to the arbitrator.
who: Every Discord user, especially people who post in large or public servers, and U.S. and Canadian users bound by Discord's arbitration agreement
seo_title: Discord terms update Dec 15, 2026: server content in search results, new arbitration rules
seo_desc: Discord's Terms of Service, effective December 15, 2026, let server admins have server content appear off Discord, such as in search engine results; disputes now need a form at dis.gd/disputes, and the arbitrator decides arbitrability.

redline.before: Server owners and admins also control whether to make their server available in Server Discovery, whether to publish their server invite link on public websites, whether to enable community growth and safety features, and whether to add bots or other apps.
redline.after: This means that server admins can choose to enable community growth and safety features, add bots or other apps, have their servers appear on Server Discovery, have certain content from the server appear off of Discord (such as in search engine results), and publish their server invite links on public websites.
redline.label: Terms of Service · What you can expect from us
redline.note: New: admins can make server content visible outside Discord, including in search engines.

redline.before: We reserve the right to block, remove, and/or permanently delete your content if we determine it is in breach of these terms, our
redline.after: We reserve the right to block, remove, and/or permanently delete your content for any reason, including if we determine it is in breach of these terms, our
redline.label: Terms of Service · Your content
redline.note: Removal is no longer tied to a breach: Discord can delete content "for any reason".

redline.before: IF YOU’RE A U.S. OR CANADIAN RESIDENT YOU ALSO AGREE TO THE FOLLOWING “AGREEMENT TO ARBITRATE” WHICH CONTAINS MANDATORY ARBITRATION PROVISIONS.
redline.after: IF YOU’RE A U.S. OR CANADIAN RESIDENT YOU AGREE TO THE FOLLOWING “AGREEMENT TO ARBITRATE” WHICH, CONTAINS MANDATORY ARBITRATION PROVISIONS. IF YOU’RE NOT A U.S. OR CANADIAN RESIDENT, BUT CHOOSE TO INITIATE ARBITRATION, YOU ALSO AGREE TO THE FOLLOWING “AGREEMENT TO ARBITRATE” AND AGREE TO THE APPOINTMENT OF A US ARBITRATOR AND THE FOLLOWING BINDING ARBITRATION PROVISIONS.
redline.label: Terms of Service · Settling disputes
redline.note: Users outside the U.S. and Canada who start an arbitration now agree to a U.S. arbitrator and the full arbitration agreement.

actions: Before December 15, 2026, check which of your servers are in Server Discovery or have public invite links, and treat anything posted there as public
If you have a dispute with Discord, the first step is now the Dispute Resolution Form at dis.gd/disputes, not an email to disputes@discordapp.com
Read the archived and new versions at discord.com/terms; Discord says that if you keep using the service after changes take effect, "it means that you agree to the changes"
what:
Discord has posted new [Terms of Service](https://discord.com/terms) ("Last Updated: November 23, 2026", "Effective: December 15, 2026"), and they are already the version on the page.

Change 1: Server content outside Discord. The old terms said server owners and admins control "whether to make their server available in Server Discovery" and whether to publish invite links. The new terms say "Server admins decide what features their servers have and control the visibility of their servers, including the content within subject to certain user controls", and that admins can "have certain content from the server appear off of Discord (such as in search engine results)". The content section adds that server owners may "enable certain server content to appear off of Discord. Anyone can access this content." The terms do not say which servers are eligible or what the "user controls" are.

Change 2: Deleting content and accounts. Discord may now remove content "for any reason, including if we determine it is in breach of these terms", and adds "we make no promises or guarantees to you or others that we will or will not block, remove and/or permanently delete content from the services, or suspend or terminate any accounts." Account termination moves from "for any reason, or for the following reasons" to "for any reason, including but not limited to the following reasons".

Change 3: Arbitration. Before you can sue or arbitrate, the informal-dispute step now "requires submitting Discord's Dispute Resolution Form available at dis.gd/disputes completely and accurately" (it used to be an email to disputes@discordapp.com). A new "Delegation of Arbitrability" paragraph says "the arbitrator, and not any federal, state, or local court or agency, shall have exclusive authority to resolve any question, dispute, or controversy concerning the existence, scope, validity, enforceability, or applicability of this Agreement to Arbitrate". And people outside the U.S. and Canada who "CHOOSE TO INITIATE ARBITRATION" now also agree "TO THE APPOINTMENT OF A US ARBITRATOR". Each side also gets "the right to file early dispositive motions before the opening discovery in the arbitration."

Other changes: Account recovery now depends on "password recovery via the email or phone number associated with your account or multi-factor authentication methods"; a new sentence says Discord "may use automated systems to rank or show you things like notifications or sponsored content"; sponsored content is now described as "sponsored content on behalf of third parties"; the warranty disclaimer adds "WE CANNOT AND DO NOT REPRESENT OR WARRANT THAT THE SERVICES WILL ALWAYS BE SECURE OR ERROR-FREE"; and the line about Discord's list of minimum ages around the world was removed.

What stays the same: The minimum age is still 13, the class-action waiver still applies to U.S. and Canadian users, and the terms still say Discord "will provide 30 days’ notice of the date of any material changes to this Agreement to Arbitrate." Discord's privacy policy changed the same day; see our separate article.
faq: Will my Discord messages show up on Google?

Discord's new terms say server admins can "have certain content from the server appear off of Discord (such as in search engine results)". They don't say which servers qualify. Direct messages aren't mentioned; content in public or Discovery servers is the content the terms describe as accessible to anyone.
When do Discord's new terms take effect?
December 15, 2026, per the "Effective" date at the top of discord.com/terms.
How do I start a dispute with Discord now?
By "submitting Discord's Dispute Resolution Form available at dis.gd/disputes completely and accurately"; the email address disputes@discordapp.com was removed from the terms.
sources: Discord Terms of Service (Last Updated Nov 23, 2026; Effective Dec 15, 2026; fetched Nov 24)

headline: Discord's Dec 15 privacy policy adds advertising IDs for sponsored content, personalized by default in some regions
tldr: From December 15, Discord's privacy policy says sponsored content can use your device or advertising ID, and that in some regions it "may be personalized by default (and you can disable it)".
who: Discord users who see Quests or other sponsored content, and anyone asked to verify their age on Discord
seo_title: Discord privacy policy Dec 15, 2026: advertising IDs, sponsored content personalized by default
seo_desc: Discord's privacy policy, effective December 15, 2026, adds device and advertising IDs (IDFA, Android Ad ID) for sponsored content, says it may be personalized by default in some regions, and adds an age-information section.

redline.after: If you interact with sponsored content, this may also include, consistent with your settings, information like device ID, advertising ID (such as IDFA or Android Ad ID), or similar unique IDs (such as a click or interaction ID).
redline.label: Privacy Policy · Device information
redline.note: New: advertising identifiers are collected when you engage with sponsored content.

redline.after: For example, depending on where you live and how old you are, we may deliver personalized sponsored content after you provide consent. But in other regions, sponsored content may be personalized by default (and you can disable it).
redline.label: Privacy Policy · How we use your information
redline.note: Opt-in in some places, opt-out in others; the policy doesn't list which.

redline.before: You’ll also need to provide your birthday. In some cases, we may require additional information to verify your age.
redline.after: We also collect your IP address and limited device information to help us determine the region you’re in when you’re using Discord. In some cases, we may require additional information to verify your age, and the information collected depends on the age assurance method used.
redline.label: Privacy Policy · Age information

actions: Before December 15, 2026, look through Discord's privacy settings for sponsored-content personalization and turn it off if you don't want it

If you post in public or Discovery servers, assume the content may be visible off Discord: the policy now says admins control "whether the content is available off of Discord such as in search engine results"
To opt out of Discord marketing, use the "Notifications" settings in Discord or the unsubscribe link in its emails
what:
Discord's [Privacy Policy](https://discord.com/privacy) was updated the same day as its terms ("Last Updated: November 23, 2026", "Effective: December 15, 2026").

Change 1: Advertising IDs. Device information now "may also include, consistent with your settings, information like device ID, advertising ID (such as IDFA or Android Ad ID), or similar unique IDs (such as a click or interaction ID)" when you interact with sponsored content. Discord adds that "If you engage with third party sponsored content, we may receive interaction and measurement data (such as impressions, clicks, and conversions) from these sources", and that it may "use automated systems to process information about your activity or interactions with sponsored content and personalize, measure campaign performance, and prevent fraud."

Change 2: Default personalization. A new sentence says "depending on where you live and how old you are, we may deliver personalized sponsored content after you provide consent. But in other regions, sponsored content may be personalized by default (and you can disable it)." The policy doesn't name the regions.

Change 3: Age information. A new section says Discord collects "your IP address and limited device information to help us determine the region you’re in", that age-check information "depends on the age assurance method used", and that "We work with trusted providers so that Discord doesn’t handle the information you submit to confirm your age, such as a selfie, identify documents, or credit card details. Instead, Discord only collects, processes, or stores age signals (such as your age or age category)." Discord may also use information "to build or improve models that help us determine a user’s age group", and says safety laws require it to keep "logs about age signals we receive, the method used to confirm age".

Other changes: Server admins now control "whether the content is available off of Discord such as in search engine results"; Discord says it doesn't "access or store" voice and video call contents, while noting users can create Clips; billing information can include "in some cases tax information"; third-party apps can provide "analytics about your interactions with the server"; and the EU rights wording now covers the United Kingdom too.
faq: Does Discord personalize sponsored content by default?

In some regions, yes. The policy says "in other regions, sponsored content may be personalized by default (and you can disable it)"; elsewhere Discord asks for consent first, depending on where you live and how old you are.
Does Discord keep my selfie or ID for age verification?

The policy says Discord's providers handle that, so "Discord doesn’t handle the information you submit to confirm your age, such as a selfie, identify documents, or credit card details"; Discord keeps age signals such as your age or age category.
sources: Discord Privacy Policy (Last Updated Nov 23, 2026; Effective Dec 15, 2026; fetched Nov 24)
